text:
Ivy: hey everyone, first week here! trying to get my onboarding PR green but both Buildkite and GH Actions are failing. not sure who to ping for app/perm stuff. :wave:

Dan: welcome Ivy! usually those two mean either the Buildkite GitHub App isn't installed for the repo or the GH workflow is blocked from secrets. what's the repo and the errors?

Ivy: repo is github.com/redwood-inference/runner-examples (private). Buildkite log: 

```
install_buildkite_github_app: pipeline cannot access repository (403)
fatal: could not fetch refs
```

Ivy: GH Actions shows: "This workflow is not allowed to access secrets. If you recently changed repo permissions, enable the Actions permissions or add the workflow to an allowed list."

jen: ok two related things. 1) Buildkite needs the GitHub App to be installed on that repo (org admin step) OR a deploy key added. 2) GH Actions secrets are often blocked by environment protection, org allowlist, or if the run comes from a fork. Are you opening the PR from a fork or a branch in-repo?

Ivy: branch in-repo. also noticed the workflow has "runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, build]" and I think our self-hosted pool uses label "ci-build" so that might be another mismatch.

ci-bot: Note: Buildkite: pipeline "runner-examples/onboard" failed to schedule due to missing GitHub App scope for repository.

Dan: good catch on runner labels. for onboarding we change runs-on to ubuntu-latest to avoid label issues; then switch back after adding the runner labels. i'll request the Buildkite app access and add you to the infra-ci team so branch builds are trusted. give it a few minutes to propagate.

Ivy: thanks. re-ran Buildkite after the app install but now the agent fails on a git-lfs smudge: "fatal: smudge 'git-lfs smudge -- %f' returned 128"

jen: that means the agent doesn't have git-lfs installed. we usually add a small step in onboarding pipelines: `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git-lfs` before the clone or in setup. i'll push a tiny pipeline tweak.

ops-bot: FYI org policy "Allow actions and reusable workflows from: Only selected repositories" is enabled. Repos not on the allowlist will not receive org-level secrets.

Ivy: GH Action still failing for secrets even after I was added to infra-ci. it says the environment "staging" requires reviewers. i can't approve.

Dan: env protections are common cause. either a maintainer approves the environment for this run or we remove the reviewer requirement for the onboarding environment. i'll ask @jen to approve temporarily. also check repo Settings -> Actions -> Workflow permissions; needs Read and write to use certain secrets/actions.

jen: approved the environment for your PR and set the repo Actions permission to Read and write. re-run the workflow.

ci-bot: GH Action run started: checking out, picking runner ubuntu-latest (workflow file overridden for onboarding branch).

Ivy: GH Action picked up secrets and passed! Buildkite still failed earlier on LFS but after the apt install step it moved further and then failed trying to push a test image to ECR with: "AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability"

Dan: for ECR pushes the CI role needs a small set of permissions (ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, ecr:PutImage, ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, etc.). onboarding branches usually skip the push to avoid needing cloud creds. i can toggle the pipeline to skip pushes for onboarding/*.

Ivy: that would be great, I wasn't expecting cloud creds for the sample. thanks for the workaround.

ops-bot: Buildkite: pipeline updated to skip docker-push step for branches matching onboarding/* by config change.

Ivy: re-run after skipping push, both Buildkite and GH Actions passed! :tada: super helpful. can i get the onboarding CI doc link? would love a quick walkthrough.

jen: welcome again! i'll DM you docs/onboarding/ci.md and schedule a 15m overview. quick takeaways i'll add to the doc: install Buildkite GitHub App (or use deploy key), add new hires to infra-ci and wait a few minutes for propagation, check Actions env protections and workflow permissions, prefer ubuntu-latest for first-run to avoid self-hosted label mismatches, install git-lfs on agents or avoid LFS in samples, and skip cloud image pushes during onboarding.

Ivy: perfect, thanks all. ping me if you want me to update any onboarding steps in the docs as i go through them. :)
